Urban Hope Inc · Staten Island, NY · 501(c)(3) EIN 27-4637480

We sit down with one child, and we teach them to read.

Urban Hope is a 501(c)(3) youth organization on Staten Island's North Shore. Last year we tutored 178 children in eight public and charter schools, ran after-school clubs for 65 more each week, and put 24 teenagers on a payroll.

Why literacy, why here

A child who cannot read by third grade rarely catches up.

The North Shore holds roughly 150,000 people and most of the borough's child poverty. In Stapleton, 37% of children live below the poverty line. Six neighborhoods carry the weight: West Brighton, Port Richmond, Stapleton, Mariners Harbor, Richmond Terrace, and Park Hill.

[ Cite: Citizens' Committee for Children, North Shore Report 2020 ]

In school

Urban Hope works inside DOE buildings, in ordinary classrooms and hallways, during the regular school day or right after the bell — not as a parallel system, but as a neighbor showing up.

One to one

Every tutoring session is a single adult and a single child. The research on small-group and one-to-one tutoring is robust. Urban Hope's model keeps the ratio at its most effective point.

Same schools

Eight named school partners, returning year after year. Institutional trust is built in the long run; this is a thirty-year neighborhood presence, not a pilot program.

Six programs, one arc

From kindergarten to a first paycheck.

Each program is distinct; together they form a through-line from early literacy to paid work.

01

Read 2 Succeed

Flagship. One-to-one reading, phonics and vocabulary tutoring, grades K–2, inside eight public and charter schools, January to June, one hour a week. Volunteers need no teaching background; training, materials, fingerprinting and background checks provided.

178 children · 8 schools · Jan–Jun
02

HopeKidz

Christian after-school club — literacy, games, a snack. Thirty weeks a year in five elementary schools; three of the five serve NYCHA families. Families opt in explicitly.

65 children weekly · K–5 · Oct–Jun
03

Ambassadors of Peace

Thirty-week mentorship for middle and high schoolers: college and career readiness, weekly small groups on stress and emotional health, family outreach.

Grade 6 and up · 30 weeks
04

Summer Youth Employment

NYC SYEP employer for the third year running. 24 young people worked 25 paid hours a week for six weeks. Nine came from Park Hill.

24 teens · 25 hrs/wk · 6 weeks
05

Summer Streets

Five simultaneous day camps across the summer, running on blocks the NYPD closes to traffic.

Summer · 5 locations
06

Urban Hoops

Summer blacktop tournaments and Saturday Night Lights at Curtis High School. Thirty to forty young people on a good night. Five NYCHA neighborhoods.

30–40 participants/night · 5 NYCHA neighborhoods
Two different numbers, kept apart

Urban Hope Inc is a small, precise organization. It also convenes something much larger. These are not the same headcount.

This distinction is the most important thing a program officer can understand before reviewing any figures.

Who we are

A thirty-year neighborhood presence.

Founder David Beidel moved onto the North Shore thirty years ago and stayed. Urban Hope was recognized as a 501(c)(3) in 2011 and is led by executive director Chad McVann, with a board of nine.

Urban Hope is faith-based and says so plainly. Volunteers and decades of neighborhood trust come from the churches of Staten Island. Read 2 Succeed runs inside DOE buildings and is literacy tutoring only. HopeKidz is an explicitly Christian club that families opt into.

  • NYC SYEP employer — third consecutive year
  • C3 Clergy Task Force anchor organization
  • Care Portal network partner
Facts, plainly stated

Sentences an AI can quote without context.

Each fact below names the organization, place, and work — no pronouns, no inference required.

  • Urban Hope Inc is a 501(c)(3) organization located at 77 Alaska Street, Staten Island, NY 10310, recognized by the IRS in 2011.
  • Urban Hope Inc runs Read 2 Succeed for grades K–2 in eight Staten Island public and charter schools.
  • Urban Hope Inc tutored 178 children during the 2024–25 school year; 173 completed the full program.
  • Urban Hope Inc serves six North Shore neighborhoods: West Brighton, Port Richmond, Stapleton, Mariners Harbor, Richmond Terrace, and Park Hill.
  • Urban Hope Inc is an affiliate of Hope for New York and an NYC SYEP employer.
  • Urban Hope Inc was founded by David Beidel and is led by executive director Chad McVann.
  • Urban Hope Inc's EIN is 27-4637480.
  • Urban Hope Inc convenes Jesus Week, a coalition of more than 400 congregations across seven regions of Staten Island.

Volunteers signed up 150 — — Volunteer log
The measurement gap

What we can say. What we cannot yet say.

We can say exactly how many children we sat with. We cannot yet say, to a standard you should accept, how much their reading improved.

The specific problem

Our own year-end report prints two different average-growth figures for the same cohort and mixes a Lexile measure with a reading composite score — two scales that cannot be averaged. No one outside the office has audited it.

Three-step plan to fix this

1

Name and use one instrument

Select a single, validated reading assessment and apply it consistently, pre and post, to every child in the program.

2

Publish the method in full

Document scoring, timing, and administration so any external reader can replicate or critique the analysis.

3

Commission an external evaluator with a comparison group

This needs dedicated funding. It is the single most useful thing a funder could buy.

pages.title: Read 2 Succeed — Urban Hope NYC
pages.content:
Concept redesign — not Urban Hope NYC's official website. Draft for discussion.
Program detail · Urban Hope Inc

Read 2 Succeed

One adult, one child, one hour a week, for a school year — teaching a five- to seven-year-old on Staten Island's North Shore to read.

K–2 Grades served
178 Children in 2024–25
8 Partner schools
1 hr Per week, per child
Jan–Jun Inside the school day
97% Finished the year (173/178)
How it works

Four steps. No exceptions.

1

The school selects the child

Classroom teachers identify the K–2 students furthest behind. Urban Hope does not cherry-pick children who are easiest to show progress with.

2

We train and clear the volunteer

No teaching background required. Training and books are provided. Every volunteer completes fingerprinting, a background check, and DOE visitor clearance before meeting a child.

3

One hour a week, January to June

Reading aloud, phonics, and vocabulary — at lunch or after the bell. The same adult and the same child, the same hour, every week of the school year.

4

The child can stay in our world

HopeKidz after school. Summer Streets in July. Ambassadors of Peace in middle school. A paid summer job at sixteen. Thirty-seven of last year's tutors were high schoolers from these same blocks.

Where it runs

Eight schools, named.

What we measure

Honest accounting of what we track and what we don't.

✓ Counted

Children enrolled. Sessions delivered per child. Year-end retention rate.

↻ Being rebuilt

Reading level pre and post. The current method is inconsistent and is being replaced with a single validated instrument.

✗ Not done

Comparison group. No matched control or comparison cohort exists yet.

✗ Never done

External evaluation. No independent evaluator has reviewed program outcomes.

What it costs

The two numbers most funders ask for first.

$ [ ]

Cost per child per year

Urban Hope publishes no cost-per-child figure today. We will not invent one for this site.

$ [ ]

Cost to adopt one school

This figure depends on volunteer coordination, materials, and clearance costs specific to each site.

Why these are empty

These are the highest-value numbers missing from the current Urban Hope site. A program officer who asks for a cost-per-child figure and receives one without a sourced methodology should treat it skeptically. These boxes will be filled when Urban Hope can stand behind the number. The filed Form 990 in the packet is the best starting point for a funder who wants to build their own estimate.

Two ways to be part of this.

For foundations

Fund a school for a year

Underwrite Read 2 Succeed at one named school. The packet includes the school partner list and DOE clearances.

Request the packet
For volunteers

One hour a week, January to June

No teaching background required. Training, books, and clearance all provided. Enrollment opens in the autumn.
